content:
Lenovo has launched a colourful new laptop, the IdeaPad Vibe, taking aim at the MacBook Neo.

Lenovo officially unveiled the IdeaPad Vibe at its Lenovo Innovation World event on the eve of IFA, clearly setting its sights on Apple's most accessible and popular MacBook Neo. Judging by the specs, this laptop can absolutely hold its own. Users can choose between 14-inch and 15-inch OLED displays; the chassis measures 14.9mm thick and starts at 2.87 pounds. While it is thicker and larger than Apple's laptop, at least the starting weight is not noticeably heavier than its rival. Lenovo says the Vibe will be available in plastic and metal chassis options.

But the design is genuinely eye-catching — Lenovo has partnered with Pantone to offer the IdeaPad Vibe in seven different colours, including:

Dreamy Purple: a soft purple tone with alluring depth, radiating a calming energy that helps you feel at ease wherever you go. Spicy Gold: a rich gold tone that blends warmth and vitality, exuding confidence and approachability. Zen Green: a nature-inspired green that radiates balance and harmony, inviting you to slow down. Icy Blue: a minimalist cool-toned blue that brings a crisp clarity and a refreshing feel. Energy Coral: a warm, uplifting colour with a touch of optimistic orange, radiating friendly positivity wherever it goes. Mystery Blue: a deep blue tone that exudes trust, confidence and elegance. Resolute Grey: a classic grey that radiates strength, composure and understated taste.

The keyboard also features swappable keycaps, allowing users to freely mix and match different colour combinations to suit their personal style.

But good looks are only the basics — Lenovo has equipped this laptop with a fairly attractive array of ports: two USB-A ports, one HDMI port, two USB-C ports, a headphone jack, and even a microSD card reader. There's also a 5-megapixel camera (with a physical privacy shutter), an optional backlit keyboard, and an optional touchscreen exclusive to the 15-inch model.

So how about the internal specs?

Users can choose between AMD Ryzen AI 400 chips and Qualcomm Snapdragon X chips. The AMD model supports up to 32GB of RAM and is user-upgradeable. Storage goes up to 1TB and is also upgradeable, with dual slots. The Snapdragon version supports up to 24GB of RAM; storage remains upgradeable, but RAM does not. Lenovo says an Intel version will arrive later.

The Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe will go on sale in two phases. The AMD model will debut in October, with the Snapdragon model following in November. Both start at $699.99 — a price point that, with Apple having raised RAM pricing, now lines up neatly with the MacBook Neo.

Lenovo also unveiled the IdeaCentre AIO I all-in-one desktop, available with 24-inch and 27-inch displays, colour options similar to the Vibe, and a starting price of $939. The product will also begin shipping in November.
